document: Comment CTA example: “Comment BLOCKER and tell me which part feels hardest right now.” Use when the post diagnoses a problem and you want useful replies.
Comment CTA example: “Comment TEMPLATE and I’ll send you the version you can adapt.” Use after a practical framework or checklist.
Comment CTA example: “Do you agree, or have you seen the opposite? Tell me below.” Use for contrarian or discussion posts.
DM keyword CTA example: “DM AUDIT and I’ll send the 5-question self-check.” Use when the next step feels private.
DM keyword CTA example: “DM PLAN and I’ll send the simple starter plan.” Use when the post promises a sequence or roadmap.
DM keyword CTA example: “DM START if you want the private checklist.” Use for sensitive goals, money, health, confidence, or business problems.
Save CTA example: “Save this for the next time you’re comparing options.” Use for buyer criteria and decision posts.
Save CTA example: “Save this checklist before you try it yourself.” Use for step-by-step posts.
Save CTA example: “Save this and revisit it when you’re planning your next [specific moment].” Use with trigger moments.
Follow CTA example: “Follow for one practical [niche] breakdown every week.” Use when the creator has a repeatable content promise.
Follow CTA example: “Follow if you want [desired identity/outcome] without [painful tradeoff].” Use for positioning-heavy posts.
Follow CTA example: “Follow for part 2, where I’ll show the exact example.” Use when the post naturally opens a series.
Download CTA example: “Download the free [resource] if you want the full version.” Use when the resource directly matches the post promise.
Download CTA example: “Grab the swipe file/template so you don’t have to start from a blank page.” Use for templates, scripts, and examples.
Download CTA example: “Use the guide first; if it helps, you’ll know what to ask for next.” Use for trust-building lead magnets.
Share CTA example: “Send this to a friend who keeps saying [audience phrase].” Use when the hook names a common frustration.
Share CTA example: “Share this with the person who helps you make this decision.” Use for business, family, team, or partner decisions.
Book/visit CTA example: “If you’re in [market], book a visit this week and we’ll help you choose the right option.” Use for local services.
Buy/order CTA example: “Order the [specific offer] if you want [specific result] without [specific friction].” Use for productized offers.

CTA matching rule: comment creates conversation, DM keyword starts a private flow, save supports utility, follow supports repeated value, download captures leads, share spreads relatability, book/visit fits local intent, buy/order fits high purchase intent.

Lead magnet CTA rule: If a saved guide exists, the CTA should name the guide and keyword clearly, for example: “Comment GUIDE and I’ll send you the free checklist.” Do not use vague CTAs when a specific resource exists.

No-guide CTA rule: If no guide or URL exists, avoid promising a download. Use a goal-based CTA such as “Comment START and I’ll send you the first step,” “Comment BOOK and I’ll send the details,” or “Comment ORDER and I’ll send the link.”
Public comment reply rule: Keep the public reply short and natural: “Sent it,” “I’ll DM it now,” “Sending the details,” or “Check your DMs.” The real value should be in the private message.
